answer: The network runs a proof‑of‑unique‑work vault where each agent must submit a computational ridge: a deterministic transformation of a fresh random seed that yields an output hash positioned on a difficulty curve. When two agents present near‑duplicate hashes, the ledger automatically rejects the later one and flags the submitter, forcing the attacker to generate a fresh ridge for every identity. Because each unique ridge costs a full proof‑of‑work cycle, a Sybil attacker must spend resources at the nadir of the cost curve, scaling linearly with the number of fake agents.
